summary: Three good passages of the right length (871 / 823 / 870 words), on the history of board games, car-sharing cooperatives, and why time seems to speed up with age. Difficulty rises properly and Passage 3 is real C1 academic writing. It is a little gentler than IELTS because the Passage 1 gap sentences and the final word-list summary stay very close to the passage's wording, which suits B2 students.
strengths: Full IELTS mix: sentence completion, T/F/NG, matching information, summary completion, matching people with one extra name, MCQ, Y/N/NG and a word-list summary.

T/F/NG and Y/N/NG items are sound: FALSE items are clearly contradicted (Q9 'ordinary soldiers played it too', Q12 'competed to sound improving') and NOT GIVEN items are genuinely not addressed (Q10 Go in Europe, Q33 technology).
Passage 3 MCQ distractors are well made: Q27 option A echoes 'broad curve of the complaint' while reversing it; Q29 option D contradicts 'much-repeated experiment'.
All keys checked and correct; completion answers are copied from the passage and inside the word limit; completion and T/F/NG answers follow passage order.

issues.problem: The paraphrase pair used 'little used', which is not in the question ('how little the typical private car is actually used').
issues.change: Pair is now ['ninety-five per cent of its life parked', 'how little the typical private car is actually used'].

issues.problem: Some existing pairs were weak one-word matches (Q24 'a visible price'/'a price', Q25 'a lifeline'/'matter most', Q26 'Members stay'/'stay committed', Q28 'races by'/'feels brief').
issues.change: Replaced with the paraphrase that actually decides the answer, e.g. Q25 ['a marginal market to a company', 'places firms find unprofitable'], Q26 ['Customers leave the moment a cheaper offer appears', 'ordinary customers would walk away'].

issues.problem: Several Passage 1 completion sentences repeat the passage's own words around the gap (Q4 'Persian expression about a helpless ______', Q5 'new powers', Q7 'printing method called ______'), so they can be answered by matching words.
issues.change: Suggest more paraphrase around the gaps, e.g. Q4 'In Persian, the term checkmate originally referred to a powerless ______.'

issues.problem: The word-list summary (Q36-40) follows the passage's sentences closely ('the life we have lived', 'remembered past', 'thickens the record'), which makes it easier than an IELTS summary.
issues.change: Suggest rewording the summary lines so they paraphrase the passage, keeping the same answers.

issues.problem: Q12 and Q32 have no clean same-meaning pair (the passage contradicts the statement rather than restating it), so they are left without a pair.
